gaps: How the harness-owned manifest scopes .codex/agents: agents carry no canon markers (only skills do), so enumerating them in a strict whitelist adds drift for no bug-fixing benefit, while omitting them lets a client's custom agent be vendored into a scaffold.
resolutions: Human ruling: FILTER SKILLS ONLY. The manifest scopes the harness-owned skill (forge, under .claude/skills and .codex/skills); .codex/agents and .codex config copy as-is. This closes the actual dangling-canon bug (skills are the canon-marker carriers) without agent-list drift; a client's custom agent landing in a scaffold is cosmetic, not breaking, and is an accepted trade. Folded into Technical Approach and Risks; AC1 already scopes the filter to skills.
summary: The plan applies the confirmed spec: init and adopt route their .claude/.codex skill vendoring through one shared harness-owned definition (upgrade's CLAUDE_HARNESS_OWNED, now shared), copying only skills/forge and never the source's other skills, while agents/config copy as-is; and the FORGE-INIT-1 fixture-bound tests gain a presence-keyed skip so the vendored suite passes in a client and still runs here. Root cause verified in code (all three commands source from repo_root()). The one open scope decision (agents) was put to the human and resolved. No contradiction with active decisions (0016 machinery ownership is the basis; 0028 boundary helpers are reused unchanged). Ready for plan-mode approval.
